CVE-2012-5134.patch_commit_message: Fix potential out of bound access

behavior_changes: Pre-patch: if len became zero, the loop condition evaluated buf[-1], causing an out-of-bounds heap read and potential denial of service or code execution.
Post-patch: when len == 0, the loop exits immediately and no out-of-bounds access occurs.
Post-patch: trailing spaces are still removed for non-empty values, but the trimming loop never indexes before the buffer start.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: All accesses to buf through len - 1 occur only when len is strictly positive, thereby preventing heap buffer underreads.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch adds a len > 0 check to the trailing-space trim loop, preventing the loop from evaluating buf[len - 1] when len is zero.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In xmlParseAttValueComplex, the trailing-space trimming loop accessed buf[len - 1] without first checking len > 0. When len reached zero, the next loop condition evaluated buf[-1], causing a heap buffer underflow / out-of-bounds read before the allocated buffer.

CVE-2013-0338.patch_commit_message:
Detect excessive entities expansion upon replacement

If entities expansion in the XML parser is asked for,
it is possble to craft relatively small input document leading
to excessive on-the-fly content generation.
This patch accounts for those replacement and stop parsing
after a given threshold. it can be bypassed as usual with the
HUGE parser option.

new_lines: * We are copying here, make sure there is no abuse
* We are copying here, make sure there is no abuse
* If the volume of entity copy reaches 10 times the
* amount of parsed data and over the large text threshold
* then that's very likely to be an abuse.

behavior_changes: ctxt->sizeentcopy is initialized to 0 in xmlInitParserCtxt and reset to 0 in xmlCtxtReset.
xmlParserEntityCheck signature is extended with a replacement parameter; callers in xmlParseReference and xmlStringLenDecodeEntities are updated.

New check: if replacement != 0 and replacement < XML_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH, return 0; otherwise compute consumed as input->consumed + (input->cur - input->base) + ctxt->sizeentities and return 0 if replacement < XML_PARSER_NON_LINEAR * consumed; otherwise fall through to fatal XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP.

In xmlParseReference, before copying entity child nodes, ctxt->sizeentcopy is incremented by ent->length, and the new check with replacement=ctxt->sizeentcopy is performed; if it fails, parsing returns early.
In xmlStringLenDecodeEntities, calls to xmlParserEntityCheck now pass 0 as the replacement argument, preserving the old size-based checks for that path.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Bounded resource consumption during internal entity expansion by limiting the total volume of entity replacement text copied relative to parsed input; prevent entity-expansion amplification attacks.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: Add a per-parser counter (sizeentcopy) that accumulates the length of entity replacement content copied during entity expansion. Extend xmlParserEntityCheck to accept a replacement size and abort parsing with XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP when the cumulative copied entity bytes exceed both a fixed large-text threshold and a dynamic threshold proportional to consumed input unless the HUGE option is set.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The parser did not track or limit the cumulative size of entity replacement text copied during internal entity expansion. The existing xmlParserEntityCheck considered only parsed input size and entity counts, not the total bytes of entity content copied into the document tree. An attacker could declare one long entity and reference it many times, causing the parser to copy the long replacement text repeatedly while never exceeding the old size/entity-count thresholds, leading to excessive CPU and memory consumption.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: In the pre-patch xmlParseReference, branches that copied entity child nodes into the document or reader tree did not accumulate the length of copied entity content and did not call xmlParserEntityCheck for copy-volume abuse. The old xmlParserEntityCheck signature accepted only (ctxt, size, ent) and could not evaluate replacement-copy amplification. It relied on entity counts and parsed data density, so an entity with a long replacement text and many references remained under the radar. The parser kept allocating and copying text/child structures for each reference, yielding linear amplification to unbounded output.

CVE-2013-0339.patch_commit_message:
Do not fetch external parsed entities

Unless explicietely asked for when validating or replacing entities
with their value. Problem pointed out by Tom Lane <tgl@redhat.com>

* parser.c: do not load external parsed entities unless needed
* test/errors/extparsedent.xml result/errors/extparsedent.xml*:
  add a regression test to avoid change of the behaviour in the future

new_lines: * Note: external parsed entities will not be loaded, it is not
* required for a non-validating parser, unless the parsing option
* of validating, or substituting entities were given. Doing so is
* far more secure as the parser will only process data coming from

behavior_changes: The condition to parse an entity changed from `ent->checked == 0` to `ent->checked == 0 && (ent->etype != XML_EXTERNAL_GENERAL_PARSED_ENTITY || (ctxt->options & (XML_PARSE_NOENT | XML_PARSE_DTDVALID)))`.
When an external general parsed entity is encountered without `XML_PARSE_NOENT` or `XML_PARSE_DTDVALID`, the code no longer calls `xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate` for that entity.
Skipped external entities remain unparsed, so the function falls through and may emit only a SAX `reference` callback without fetching external data.
External entities are still loaded when `XML_PARSE_NOENT` or `XML_PARSE_DTDVALID` is set, preserving explicit substitution and validation behavior.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: A non-validating parser must not dereference external parsed entities by default; external entity expansion is opt-in through `XML_PARSE_NOENT` or `XML_PARSE_DTDVALID`.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch restricts external parsed entity loading to explicit modes: either entity substitution (`XML_PARSE_NOENT`) or DTD validation (`XML_PARSE_DTDVALID`). By default, external general parsed entities are not fetched.

root_cause_analysis.summary: Pre-patch xmlParseReference would parse any referenced entity whose `ent->checked` was zero, including external general parsed entities, leading to default fetching and expansion of external resources.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: The entity parsing gate was only `if (ent->checked == 0)`, so when an `XML_EXTERNAL_GENERAL_PARSED_ENTITY` was referenced, the code called `xmlParseExternalEntityPrivate` without requiring `XML_PARSE_NOENT` or `XML_PARSE_DTDVALID`, allowing XXE, file reads, and SSRF.

CVE-2013-0339.vulnerability_description: libxml2 through 2.9.1 does not properly handle external entities expansion unless an application developer uses the xmlSAX2ResolveEntity or xmlSetExternalEntityLoader function, which allows remote attackers to cause a denial of service (resource consumption), send HTTP requests to intranet servers, or read arbitrary files via a crafted XML document, aka an XML External Entity (XXE) issue. CVE-2014-3660.patch_commit_message:
Fix missing entities after CVE-2014-3660 fix

For https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=738805

The fix for CVE-2014-3660 introduced a regression in some case
where entity substitution is required and the entity is used
first in anotther entity referenced from an attribute value

behavior_changes: Old: only (ent->checked == 0) allowed entering the entity check/parse block; entities already checked but without children were skipped.
New: condition becomes (ent->checked == 0) || ((ent->children == NULL) && (ctxt->options & XML_PARSE_NOENT)), so NOENT-mode no-children entities are re-parsed.
Old: such entities could leave ent->children == NULL and result in unresolved or missing entity references from attribute-value entities.
New: when expanded in the block, ent->checked is recomputed and ent->children may be populated, making subsequent references consistent.
The external-general-entity gate and xmlParserEntityCheck call remain inside the block, so the CVE-2014-3660 DoS protections remain enforced.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Correct entity expansion under XML_PARSE_NOENT without reintroducing unbounded nested-entity expansion; expansion remains bounded by entity count and loop checks.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch relaxes the entity parsing gate to also enter the parse/check block when ent->children == NULL and XML_PARSE_NOENT is set, restoring required entity substitution while preserving the entity-expansion limits introduced for CVE-2014-3660.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The pre-patch condition in xmlParseReference only enters the entity parsing/checking block when ent->checked == 0. Under XML_PARSE_NOENT, an entity can be marked checked but still have no cached children, especially when first referenced from another entity used in an attribute value. In that state the parser skips required substitution, producing missing entity content. This is the regression introduced by the CVE-2014-3660 entity-expansion fix.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Overly restrictive gating of entity expansion: the condition (ent->checked == 0) does not allow re-entry for ent->children == NULL cases in NOENT mode, so entity substitution is silently omitted even though the caller requires it. The entity count and loop protections remain in the skipped block, so this is primarily a correctness/security-control regression in entity-expansion handling.

CVE-2015-5312.patch_commit_message:
CVE-2015-5312 Another entity expansion issue

For https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=756733
It is one case where the code in place to detect entities expansions
failed to exit when the situation was detected, leading to DoS
Problem reported by Kostya Serebryany @ Google
Patch provided by David Drysdale @ Google

behavior_changes: Old behavior: after xmlParseStringEntityRef() returned, the function unconditionally proceeded to xmlParserEntityCheck(ctxt, 0, ent, 0) and later recursive calls, even when ctxt->lastError.code indicated XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP or XML_ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR.

New behavior: immediately after xmlParseStringEntityRef(), the function checks whether ctxt->lastError.code is XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP or XML_ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR; if true, it jumps to int_error and returns failure.
Net effect: entity expansion that is detected as looping or internally erroneous now terminates instead of continuing CPU-bound work.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: The parser fails closed on entity expansion loop or internal error conditions, ensuring expansion limits are enforced and cannot be bypassed by ignoring parser error state.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: Add an explicit check of ctxt->lastError.code immediately after xmlParseStringEntityRef() and before any entity processing. If the parser has already flagged XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP or XML_ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR, the function jumps to int_error and aborts further expansion.

root_cause_analysis.summary: xmlStringLenDecodeEntities parses entity reference strings and recursively expands them. Before the patch, after xmlParseStringEntityRef() signaled a fatal entity-loop or internal parser error by setting ctxt->lastError.code, the function did not inspect the error code and continued into entity processing and recursive expansion. This defeated the entity-expansion loop detection, allowing crafted XML to force unbounded entity expansion and CPU exhaustion.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Missing error-state propagation and early exit after xmlParseStringEntityRef(). When entity expansion limits are exceeded, the parser sets ctxt->lastError.code to XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP or XML_ERR_INTERNAL_ERROR, but the caller ignores this error, proceeds with xmlParserEntityCheck(ctxt, 0, ent, 0), and then recurses into xmlStringDecodeEntities(). The loop guard is not enforced, enabling continued entity expansion despite detection.

CVE-2015-5312.vulnerability_description: The xmlStringLenDecodeEntities function in parser.c in libxml2 before 2.9.3 does not properly prevent entity expansion, which allows context-dependent attackers to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption) via crafted XML data, a different vulnerability than CVE-2014-3660.

CVE-2015-7497.patch_commit_message:
CVE-2015-7497 Avoid an heap buffer overflow in xmlDictComputeFastQKey

For https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=756528
It was possible to hit a negative offset in the name indexing
used to randomize the dictionary key generation
Reported and fix provided by David Drysdale @ Google

behavior_changes: Old: if len > 10, directly evaluate `value += name[len - (plen + 1 + 1)]`, even if the index is negative.
New: compute `offset = len - (plen + 1 + 1)`; if `offset < 0`, set `offset = len - (10 + 1)`; then add `name[offset]`.
For inputs where the old computed offset is non-negative, the hash value is unchanged.
For inputs that previously produced a negative offset, the new code reads from a safe fallback offset instead of performing an out-of-bounds read.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Every computed index into the heap-allocated name buffer must be non-negative before use; no negative offset can reach the buffer access in the QName hash computation.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch introduces an offset variable and clamps it to a safe fallback value `len - (10 + 1)` whenever the original computed offset is negative, ensuring the `name[offset]` access stays within bounds.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In xmlDictComputeFastQKey, when len > 10, the pre-patch code computes an array index into the heap-allocated name buffer as len - (plen + 2) without checking whether the result is non-negative. If the prefix length is large enough relative to len, the index becomes negative, causing an out-of-bounds heap read before the name buffer.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Direct use of a potentially negative computed offset `name[len - (plen + 1 + 1)]` as an array index into a heap-allocated buffer, with no lower-bound validation.

Avoid processing entities after encoding conversion failures

For https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=756527
and was also raised by Chromium team in the past

When we hit a convwersion failure when switching encoding
it is bestter to stop parsing there, this was treated as a
fatal error but the parser was continuing to process to extract
more errors, unfortunately that makes little sense as the data
is obviously corrupt and can potentially lead to unexpected behaviour.

behavior_changes: xmlSwitchEncoding now calls xmlSwitchToEncodingInt, stores the result, and if the result is negative or ctxt->errNo is XML_I18N_CONV_FAILED, calls xmlStopParser(ctxt) and sets ctxt->errNo = XML_I18N_CONV_FAILED.

patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch makes encoding conversion failures fatal and immediate: xmlSwitchEncoding now stops the parser via xmlStopParser and forces ctxt->errNo to XML_I18N_CONV_FAILED when conversion fails. xmlParseXMLDecl and xmlParseDocument then check for XML_PARSER_EOF (in addition to XML_ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ENCODING) and return before further processing.

CVE-2015-7500.patch_commit_message:
CVE-2015-7500 Fix memory access error due to incorrect entities boundaries

For https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=756525
handle properly the case where we popped out of the current entity
while processing a start tag
Reported by Kostya Serebryany @ Google

This slightly modifies the output of 754946 in regression tests

new_lines: int i, j, nbNs, attval, oldline, oldcol, inputNr;
old_lines: int i, j, nbNs, attval, oldline, oldcol;

new_lines: * We can't switch from one entity to another in the middle
"Start tag doesn't start and stop in the same entity\n");

behavior_changes: Old: only `ctxt->input->base != base` was tested before `goto base_changed`; New: every such test is extended with `|| (inputNr != ctxt->inputNr)`.

Old: an entity change could go unnoticed and execution would fall through to restore saved `cur`, `line`, and `col` on the new input; New: when `inputNr != ctxt->inputNr`, the function calls `xmlFatalErrMsg` with `XML_ERR_ENTITY_BOUNDARY` and returns NULL.
Old: no explicit entity-boundary error for start tags; New: a fatal error message "Start tag doesn't start and stop in the same entity" is emitted when the boundary condition is detected.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: A start tag must begin and end in the same parser input entity; no buffer offset or lexical state from one entity may be reused after another entity has been selected.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch records `ctxt->inputNr` at entry to `xmlParseStartTag2` and adds it to every guard that previously only compared `base`. If the input number changes, the parser emits `XML_ERR_ENTITY_BOUNDARY` with a fatal error and aborts rather than attempting to restore and reparse across entity boundaries.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In xmlParseStartTag2, the parser saved only the current input buffer base pointer (`base`) and used it to detect whether the input had changed while parsing a start tag. It did not track the current input stream/entity number (`ctxt->inputNr`). When an entity boundary was crossed and the parser returned to a different input with the same base pointer, the stale-offset restoration `ctxt->input->cur = ctxt->input->base + cur` was performed on the wrong buffer, leading to out-of-bounds heap reads.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Insufficient input identity check: old guards only compared `ctxt->input->base != base`, so an entity pop/switch that changed `ctxt->inputNr` but left `base` unchanged was not detected. The saved lexical offset `cur` from the original entity was then applied to the current entity buffer.

patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch conditions NEXTL(len) on successful parsing of the character range, so an invalid range no longer consumes a character and the parser can propagate the error safely.

root_cause_analysis.summary: xmlFAParseCharRange advanced the parser cursor with NEXTL(len) even when parsing a character range failed, allowing a malformed XML regex to move ctxt->cur past the end of the input buffer. CVE-2017-16932.patch_commit_message:
Detect infinite recursion in parameter entities

When expanding a parameter entity in a DTD, infinite recursion could
lead to an infinite loop or memory exhaustion.

Thanks to Wei Lei for the first of many reports.

Fixes bug 759579.

behavior_changes: Old behavior: xmlPushInput() always pushed the supplied input without checking ctxt->inputNr.

New behavior: xmlPushInput() checks ((ctxt->inputNr > 40) && !(ctxt->options & XML_PARSE_HUGE)) || (ctxt->inputNr > 1024); if true, it reports XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP, pops input streams until ctxt->inputNr == 1, and returns -1.
New behavior: xmlParsePEReference() checks the return value of xmlPushInput(); on failure it frees the input stream and returns instead of continuing with an invalid/leaked input.
Security consequence: recursive parameter entity expansion is stopped deterministically instead of looping or exhausting memory.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Bounded recursion depth for parameter entity expansion; no entity expansion may push more than 40 nested inputs in normal mode or 1024 in XML_PARSE_HUGE mode.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch adds a parser input depth limit in xmlPushInput() to detect and abort excessive parameter entity nesting, and updates xmlParsePEReference() to free the newly allocated input stream when xmlPushInput() fails.

root_cause_analysis.summary: The pre-patch xmlPushInput() did not limit the parser input stack depth when expanding parameter entities. A recursive or mutually recursive parameter entity declaration could therefore push an unbounded number of input streams, causing infinite recursion or memory exhaustion.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: xmlPushInput() unconditionally called inputPush() for every entity input stream created by xmlParsePEReference(), without examining ctxt->inputNr or emitting XML_ERR_ENTITY_LOOP. Recursive parameter entity references drove ctxt->inputNr upward without any depth cap until resources were exhausted.

CVE-2017-16932.vulnerability_description: parser.c in libxml2 before 2.9.5 does not prevent infinite recursion in parameter entities.

CVE-2018-14404.patch_commit_message:
Fix nullptr deref with XPath logic ops

If the XPath stack is corrupted, for example by a misbehaving extension
function, the "and" and "or" XPath operators could dereference NULL
pointers. Check that the XPath stack isn't empty and optimize the
logic operators slightly.

Closes: https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/issues/5

Also see
https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=901817
https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=1595985

This is CVE-2018-14404.

Thanks to Guy Inbar for the report.

behavior_changes: Old behavior: arg1 = valuePop(ctxt); arg1->boolval &= arg2->boolval; valuePush(ctxt, arg1);
New behavior: if (ctxt->value != NULL) ctxt->value->boolval &= arg2->boolval; (and analogously for |=).
The new code no longer pops the first operand from the stack and no longer pushes a result back; it updates the value in place only when the stack is non-empty.
If ctxt->value is NULL, the operation is skipped rather than crashing.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Ensure that XPath logic operator evaluation never dereferences a NULL XPath value from a corrupted or empty value stack.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: For the logic operators XPATH_OP_AND and XPATH_OP_OR, operate directly on the current top-of-stack value (ctxt->value) after evaluating the second operand, and guard the boolean update with a NULL check on ctxt->value. This avoids popping and re-pushing the first operand and prevents a NULL dereference when the stack is empty.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In xmlXPathCompOpEval, the XPATH_OP_AND and XPATH_OP_OR cases unconditionally popped an XPath object with valuePop(ctxt) and then dereferenced arg1->boolval. If the value stack is empty or corrupted (for example, by a misbehaving extension function or invalid XPath expression), valuePop returns NULL, causing a NULL pointer dereference.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Unchecked result of valuePop(ctxt) is dereferenced as arg1->boolval without verifying that arg1 is non-NULL.

CVE-2020-7595.patch_commit_message:
Fix infinite loop in xmlStringLenDecodeEntities

When ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF,xmlParseStringEntityRef
return NULL which cause a infinite loop in xmlStringLenDecodeEntities

Found with libFuzzer.

Signed-off-by: Zhipeng Xie <xiezhipeng1@huawei.com>

behavior_changes: Pre-patch: loop continues if `c != 0`, `c != end`, `c != end2`, and `c != end3` are all true, even if `ctxt->instate == XML_PARSER_EOF`.
Post-patch: loop condition additionally requires `ctxt->instate != XML_PARSER_EOF`.

When EOF is encountered with a non-sentinel current character, the post-patch loop exits instead of repeatedly re-evaluating the same input character through entity parsing calls that return NULL without advancing the input.
This prevents the reported CWE-835 infinite loop.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Termination / availability: guarantee that xmlStringLenDecodeEntities exits when the parser state is EOF, preventing an infinite loop and denial of service.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: Add `ctxt->instate != XML_PARSER_EOF` to the while loop condition so the entity decoding loop exits immediately when the parser reaches EOF state.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In xmlStringLenDecodeEntities, the main decoding loop did not check whether the parser context had entered XML_PARSER_EOF. When EOF was reached, xmlParseStringEntityRef could return NULL without advancing the input pointer, leaving the current character unchanged and causing the loop to spin indefinitely.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Missing XML_PARSER_EOF check in the loop termination condition. The loop relied only on `c != 0`, `c != end`, `c != end2`, and `c != end3`; at EOF, entity/char-ref parsing failure returns NULL without consuming input, so `c` never changes and the loop makes no progress.

CVE-2020-7595.vulnerability_description: xmlStringLenDecodeEntities in parser.c in libxml2 2.9.10 has an infinite loop in a certain end-of-file situation.

CVE-2023-28484.patch_commit_message:
[CVE-2023-28484] Fix null deref in xmlSchemaFixupComplexType

Fix a null pointer dereference when parsing (invalid) XML schemas.

Thanks to Robby Simpson for the report!

Fixes #491.

behavior_changes: When baseType->subtypes is NULL and dummySequence is false, control now skips the block that calls xmlSchemaAddParticle and reads minOccurs/maxOccurs/children from baseType->subtypes.
The code instead reaches the final else branch, which does not dereference baseType->subtypes, avoiding the invalid read.
Valid schemas with non-NULL baseType->subtypes follow the same path as before; only the previously crashing invalid case is redirected to a safe path.
patch_intent_analysis.intended_security_property: Memory safety: no NULL pointer dereference while inheriting/copying complex type particle content in xmlSchemaFixupComplexType.
patch_intent_analysis.summary: The patch adds baseType->subtypes != NULL to the branch condition so the sequence-particle copy block is only entered when the base type actually has a particle to copy; otherwise control falls through to the existing empty/else path.

root_cause_analysis.summary: In xmlSchemaFixupComplexType, when fixing up a complex type derived from a base type that has no particle content (baseType->subtypes == NULL) and dummySequence is false, the parser enters a branch that treats baseType->subtypes as a valid xmlSchemaParticlePtr and dereferences it without a NULL check, causing a NULL pointer dereference for crafted invalid XSD schemas.
root_cause_analysis.unsafe_mechanism: Missing NULL guard on baseType->subtypes before casting it to xmlSchemaParticlePtr and reading ((xmlSchemaParticlePtr) baseType->subtypes)->minOccurs and ->maxOccurs. The vulnerable branch is gated only by (!dummySequence), so a NULL base particle reaches the dereference.

CVE-2023-28484.vulnerability_description: In libxml2 before 2.10.4, parsing of certain invalid XSD schemas can lead to a NULL pointer dereference and subsequently a segfault. This occurs in xmlSchemaFixupComplexType in xmlschemas.c.
